stances_toward.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded reluctant_ally - co-members of NATO/EU with visible friction are allies by necessity, not rivals (ONTOLOGY scale). Both are NATO members (the dataset floor would be 'ally'), but the bilateral file is frozen: the maritime delimitation lapsed when Albania's Constitutional Court annulled the 2009 agreement and the 2020 pledge to go to the ICJ was never executed (Greek sources said in 2026 it is 'no longer among the immediate priorities'); the Beleri conviction (Mar 2024) froze relations and Mitsotakis tied Albania's EU path to it; the Greek 'law of war' is formally in place. Rama at Delphi in 2026 spoke of a new strategic partnership within the year, which the Tirana Times calls aspirational. 'Rival' is the friction grade, not hostility: trade and tourism are dense, the 1996 friendship treaty stands, and the Delphi Declaration 2026 supports accelerating accession. No source says 'rival': our reading (confidence C). Bond none: no kinship, a recognised Greek minority.

stances_toward.note: NATO and EU co-members with no standing quarrel: Mitsotakis, the first European leader to visit Radev's Sofia (4 Jun 2026), pledged help with airspace protection and defence cooperation, the Vertical Corridor and the IGB (Greece built it when Bulgaria urgently needed gas) tie the two grids together; the only open file is the long-term waters agreement on the Arda, Maritsa and Mesta. Warming because the new cabinet chose Athens for its first European visit and both lean on the same energy corridor. Bond - affinity: Orthodox neighbours, no territorial quarrel; Athens also guards a name dispute with Skopje, where the two share a position.

stances_toward.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded reluctant_ally - co-members of NATO/EU with visible friction are allies by necessity, not rivals (ONTOLOGY scale). Prespa Agreement in force since February 2019; Greece is a NATO co-member, a major investor and the partner of the Gevgelija-Negotino gas interconnector and the Markova Noga-Lemos border crossing (Commission: cooperation 'intensified'). But Athens holds the other veto: it accuses Mickoski and President Siljanovska-Davkova of 'flagrant violation' by using 'Macedonia' in domestic contexts, says it will not ratify three cooperation memoranda until Skopje complies, and the government spokesman again tied the EU road to Greece in early October 2026. Partner rather than ally despite common NATO membership (the dataset would derive 'ally'): the name is a standing grievance and Mickoski treats Prespa as a mistake he will not repeat. Not rival, because the cooperation on energy and borders is real and Skopje asks for 'unconditional' Greek support. Trend cooling: 2024-26 friction, nothing resolved.

stances_toward.note: NATO and EU co-member; the link that counts is energy: Greek LNG and Revithoussa feed the Vertical Gas Corridor north through Bulgaria into Romania and on to Moldova and Ukraine (Greece-Bulgaria capacity about 3 bcm a year, 5 bcm possible). Confidence C: the 2025-26 sources describe the corridor, not a bilateral Romania-Greece act, and no friction was found. Bond - affinity: Orthodox neighbourhood, shared Black Sea-Aegean transport axis.

stances_toward.note: NATO co-members with friction are reluctant_ally, never rival (ontology rule), even though the dispute is the oldest in the alliance: the 1995 casus belli over any Greek extension of territorial waters beyond 6 nm, continental-shelf and EEZ claims, demilitarisation of the islands. The 2023-26 détente was real (Erdogan hosted Mitsotakis in Ankara on 11 Feb 2026, 'open and sincere', no agreements), but the 15 Aug 2026 marine-park decrees around Lemnos-Samothrace and Kastellorizo and the Blue Homeland law due in October turn the trend to cooling. Athens is also the main brake on Turkey's EU files. Bond - grievance: the Aegean, Cyprus and the minorities.

relations_to.summary: The Greece-Bulgaria interconnector (IGB, 3 bcm a year, operational October 2022) links Bulgaria to Greek LNG at Alexandroupolis and Revithoussa and to Azerbaijani gas arriving through Greece; Mitsotakis (4 Jun 2026) said Greece completed it when Bulgaria urgently needed gas in the first year of Russia's war.
relations_to.note: The 3 bcm a year capacity and the October 2022 start come from search-engine summaries of energy-trade reporting, not from the BTA article, which only confirms that Greece completed the link.

relations_to.summary: Mitsotakis visited Radev in Sofia on 4 Jun 2026, the first European leader to do so: Greek help with Bulgaria's airspace protection, deeper defence cooperation, the Vertical Gas Corridor, a long-term agreement on the Arda, Maritsa and Mesta waters, a joint trip to Montenegro on Western Balkans enlargement.

relations_to.summary: Greek government spokesman Marinakis said on 11 Jul 2024 that, as long as Skopje does not respect agreements, its 'European perspective will remain closed'; Mitsotakis said Greece would not seek ratification of three cooperation memoranda until Skopje fully complies with Prespa. In early October 2026 Athens again said North Macedonia's road to Europe runs through Greece.
